newsitem.title: USA: Aliant raises special phone service rates.
newsitem.headline: Aliant raises special phone service rates.

text.p: Aliant Communications Inc said Monday it filed a notice with the Nebraska Public Service Commission to increase rates for several optional services effective July 1.
The company said custom calling services including call waiting, three-way calling and call forwarding will be raised by a range of $0.75 to $0.90 a month, depending on the service.
In Lincoln, for example, where Aliant has the majority of its lines, call waiting will increase to $3.00 from $2.10, three-way calling to $2.50 from $1.75 and call forwarding to $2.50 from $1.75.

Extended area service allowing customers unlimited calling to one or more number will increase by $1.00 to $2.00 a month in Lincoln. Enhanced local calling areas plan rates will rise to $3.00 from $2.00 for Lincoln business customers and to $1.50 from $1.00 for residential users.

Directory listing rates will rise by $0.25 a month to $1.25 for Lincoln businesses and to $1.00 for residences, and inside wire maintenance plan fees will increase by $0.50 a month to $1.00. Some basic leased telephone rates, now ranging from $2.00 to $2.75, will increase by $0.25 to $0.50 a month.
"The increases will help Aliant Communications maintain and improve its strong communications network," Frank Hilsabeck, president and chief executive of Aliant, said in a statement.
Customers will receive information in their July bills summarizing the rate increases, the company said.
Aliant is a diversified communications company.
